description: Zero-dependency, TypeScript-native browser library for creating terminal-style typing animations. Single-function API: createTyped(target, options) returns a NexTypedController for runtime control. Supports multiple strings, custom cursors, backspace/delete effects, loops, human-like timing, speed curves, shuffle, and 10+ callback hooks. ESM only, targets ES2023 + DOM APIs.
rules: nex-typed is browser-only. It uses document, window.setTimeout, and window.setInterval. Do not use it in Node.js or SSR without a DOM shim.
Always call controller.destroy() when done to prevent timer and DOM leaks. In React use useEffect cleanup, in Vue use onUnmounted, in Svelte use onDestroy.
Use pause()/resume() for temporary halts. stop() cannot be cleanly resumed — to restart, call destroy() and create a new controller with createTyped().

The entire public API is a single function: createTyped(target, options). It returns a NexTypedController object with methods like start, pause, resume, stop, destroy, backspace, deleteString, skip, goTo, setSpeed, and setCursorBlinkSpeed.
The strings option is required. All other NexTypedOptions fields are optional with sensible defaults (typeSpeed=50ms, startDelay=0, loop=false, etc.).
Cursor style option accepts either a CSS class name (string) or an inline styles object with camelCase keys that get converted to kebab-case CSS properties.
humanTypeDelay, when set, fully replaces typeSpeed for per-character random delay. It is still affected by speedProfile and pauseOnPunctuation.
The package is ESM only. Import via: import { createTyped } from 'nex-typed'.
Refer to llms.txt at the repository root for a concise API summary with inline examples. Detailed documentation lives in docs/API.md, docs/USAGE.md, and docs/EXAMPLES.md.
